pick.headline: Suicide bombers destroy US Marine and French barracks in Beirut
pick.summary: On October 23, 1983, suicide truck bombs destroyed the US Marine barracks and a French paratroop building in Beirut, killing 241 American servicemen and 58 French soldiers.
pick.significance: It was the deadliest single day for the US Marine Corps since Iwo Jima, and led to the withdrawal of the multinational force from Lebanon in 1984. US intelligence attributed it to Iranian-backed militants.
pick.fbis: The Middle East & South Asia review of October 24, 1983, led with the Beirut headquarters bombings, citing Beirut radio's toll of US Marines and French troops, a claim by an unknown Islamic group, and Jerusalem radio blaming Syria.

alternates.headline: Hungary proclaims itself a republic
alternates.summary: On October 23, 1989, the anniversary of the 1956 uprising, acting President Matyas Szuros proclaimed the Republic of Hungary, dropping 'People's' from its name.
alternates.significance: The proclamation marked Hungary's formal break with communist rule.
alternates.fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of October 23, 1989, carried a Hungarian government statement to the National Assembly that the new constitutional law declaring the Hungarian Republic would be proclaimed on October 23.
